# Introducing OpenGame OpenGame is **the first open-source Super Game Agent** — turning **DeepSeek (DSH)**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, or any of your local coding agents into an AI Unreal Engine / Unity and full-stack game studio. Go from a single idea to **AAA-grade 3D worlds** or **monetization-ready viral mini-games** in one end-to-end pipeline. - 🚀 **Build AAA-Grade 3D Games with Your Agent.** Drive full-stack 3D gameplay, art, music, and voice straight from **DeepSeek (DSH)**, **Claude**, **Codex**, or **Gemini** — from one prompt to playable 3D action, racing, and open-world games. - 🎮 **One-Click Remix & Re-style Any Game.** Start from **25 built-in playable templates** (3D, voxel, anime, pixel & 9:16 hits) with full editable source — keep proven mechanics while swapping characters, worlds, and art styles in minutes. - 💰 **Build Games That Earn: Create → Verify → Monetize.** Automated logic checks, balance simulation, headless playtesting, covers, and gameplay trailers — ship live web links, export single-file **9:16 Playable Ads**, and connect publishing paths for **WeChat Mini Games**, **TikTok**, and **Douyin**. - 🔓 **Full-Stack Open Source (BYOA + BYOK).** Code, art, video, music, voice, SFX, and Three.js 3D are all open source — plug in your favorite [local agent](#agent-wall) and own API keys, or connect [OpenDesign Go](https://go.open-design.ai/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=opengame&utm_content=readme_en) (Black Friday lowest-ever discount, with free access to **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash**, **Seedream**, and more). ## ⚡ Quick Start ### 1. details.readme:
Give your coding agent a video editor.
Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client edits your footage with local FFmpeg, then checks its own output.
No cloud · No API keys · Python standard library
What you install and what it touches

Website · Quick start · Use cases · Demos · Tools · MCP · npm

 

 

English · 日本語 · 日本語（サイト）

Use cases, end to end: a vertical short with captions · a podcast as an audiogram · cleaning a phone clip · a cut-down of a long recording · one master, several platforms · a talk from two cameras

```bash npx ffmpeg-skill ```

caption.py --animate pop --karaoke
fit.py --aspect 9:16 --fit crop

silence.py --threshold -35
loudness.py -I -14 --tp -1


Twelve clips edited by asking: colour, slow motion and reframing, a talk laid out with its slides and cut into a captioned short, a pause removed, a green-screen composite, a levelled horizon, and three phone clips (stabilised, a night shot lifted and denoised, 60 fps slowed down). Watch them (English and Japanese) · the request and the exact commands. Nine clips are AI-generated with Google Veo; three are shot on a phone.

### Review page After an edit, ask your agent for the review page ("show me the review page"), or run `npx ffmpeg-skill review project.json --result run.json` yourself (`python3 scripts/_review.py` from a checkout). It writes one local HTML file. It shows the sources, every step with its checks, the result in a phone frame with the platform's safe area, and a timeline. Press the number of a clip or a caption, write what should change, and copy the instruction it builds back to your agent. Nothing is uploaded; the page speaks English, Japanese, Korean and Chinese.


The talk above as a vertical short, on the review page (AI-generated footage).

Left half is the input, right half is what the command produced. **[Every before/after demo, with the exact command under each one →](docs/demos.md)** — all of it built by `python3 demos/build.py`, so you can rebuild every frame of it yourself. The pictures come from [demos/footage/](demos/footage/README.md): clips AI-generated with Google Veo (the people and places do not exist) and a few shot on a phone. The sound is synthetic, and a few demos (HDR10, a panorama) use a synthetic picture. `ffmpeg-skill` is an [Agent Skill](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/agent-skills) for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and any agent that reads `SKILL.md`. It teaches the agent a fixed workflow (probe → edit losslessly where possible → check → verify) and ships **41 tools** that do the actual work with `ffmpeg` / `ffprobe`: cut, join, silence removal, fit to duration and aspect, captions and karaoke, overlays and motion graphics, HDR → SDR and LUTs, audio clean-up and typed dynamics, sync with drift correction, multicam, loudness, delivery checks, whole-edit project rendering, batch folders. Every tool is also callable as an MCP tool (`tools/list` advertises a core 12 by default to keep client context small, with `FFMPEG_SKILL_MCP_FULL=1` listing all 41; every tool is reachable by name through `tools/call` either way), and the whole set is described by a machine-readable contract. If `ffmpeg` and `python3` are on your PATH, it works: offline, on footage you would rather not upload. - **Protect your source files.** A destination that matches a declared input is refused. Direct edits require `--overwrite` to replace an existing output. A `batch --watch` job can replace an unchanged file it delivered on an earlier pass. The `-y` in the dry-run command takes effect only after the tool checks the destination. - **Call typed tools.** The agent supplies named options such as `--aspect 9:16` and `--fit pad`. The tool builds the FFmpeg command and filter graph. - **Verify the edit.** The tools probe the source and the written file, so the agent can check the actual duration, frame size and audio before reporting success. > **SPEC** (Self-Producing Execution Contract): each tool's `input_schema` — the part of its > contract and MCP tool definition that has to track the CLI flag-for-flag — is never > hand-authored beside the code. It is derived, at run time, from the same `argparse` parser that > already defines the CLI, and CI fails the build if any of it drifts. > → [full explanation](#what-is-spec) --- ## Standalone, and in an ecosystem **Standalone**, this is a local FFmpeg engine: probe → edit → verify, `npx ffmpeg-skill` and nothing else. No API key, no account, no other repo required. Everything above and below this section describes that standalone tool, and none of it changes if you never read the rest of this one. **In [kajisho5](https://github.com/kajisho5)'s wider video-production ecosystem**, this repo is the *hands*: it cuts, measures and exports files, and reports back in structured JSON. It does not decide what to cut, whether a deliverable is approvable, what makes a highlight interesting, or what a caption should say (the user's cue text is burned as written, never rewritten to fit) — those are a *brain*'s job, sitting in front of this engine, not inside it. | You want to... | Use | |---|---| | Cut / join / measure / export a file right now | **this repo** (`ffmpeg-skill`), standalone | | Decide cut points, approve a deliverable, plan a whole edit | [`video-production-agent`](https://github.com/kajisho5/video-production-agent) / [`AI-video-production-OS`](https://github.com/kajisho5/AI-video-production-OS) | | Build a typed editing graph across a workspace, without writing raw `ffmpeg` | [`video-editing-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/video-editing-skill) / [`audio-production-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/audio-production-skill) | | Put Remotion motion graphics (animated captions, silence jump cuts, audio-peak motion) on a real recording | [`remotion-ffmpeg-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/remotion-ffmpeg-skill): its compositions take their length, fps, frame, silences, scene cuts, audio peaks and beats from this repo's `probe.py`, `silence.py` and `scenes.py`. It verifies its render with `check.py` and `look.py`, composites a graphics layer with `overlay.py` (`--place` for its `--sparse` mode), and delivers through `render.py --template` | Other repos in the ecosystem — [`media-analysis-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/media-analysis-skill), [`transcription-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/transcription-skill), [`subtitle-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/subtitle-skill), [`thumbnail-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/thumbnail-skill), [`color-grading-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/color-grading-skill), [`motion-graphics-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/motion-graphics-skill), [`qc-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/qc-skill) — read this repo's `contract --json`, its tools' `--json` output and `doctor`, the same way any agent framework would; this repo does not call into any of them. The dependency runs one way. --- **Contents** [Standalone, and in an ecosystem](#standalone-and-in-an-ecosystem) · [Why](#why) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Design principles](#design-principles) · [Tools](#tools) · [Audio](#audio-is-a-first-class-input) · [Built for agents](#built-for-agents) · [FAQ](#faq) · [FFmpeg compatibility](#ffmpeg-compatibility) · [Tested on real footage](#tested-on-real-footage) · [Install](#install) · [Requirements](#requirements) · [Development](#development) · [Docs](#docs) --- ## Why An agent that "knows FFmpeg" still

details.readme:
One illustration in. A game character out.
A 2D sprite generator for Claude Code, isometric or side-scrolling: 8-direction walks, actions and pixel art
at your game's camera angle, a 3D shadow under every frame, the props to stand beside them -
and, with no 3D model at all, characters, monsters and townspeople drawn on a mannequin's walk.

What you can make · Characters · No 3D model · Side-scrollers · Pixel art · Props · Install · FAQ · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 日本語 · Español · Português

![GPT alone: one direction, the same leg always in front, no shadow. SpriteCast: the same character walking in eight directions on the game's floor, each with its shadow; a row of actions from the same 3D, the swing throwing water; as pixel art; and for a side-scroller, a boar, a stag, a guard and a herbalist each walking beside the mannequin it was drawn on](docs/hero.gif)

The same image model, the same character sheet. Left: GPT asked for a walk, as it came out. Right: what the 3D adds.
Bottom: a side-scroller's creatures and people, each beside the plain mannequin whose walk it was drawn on.

``` claude plugin marketplace add Sunghwan0112/spritecast claude plugin install spritecast@spritecast ``` Then just ask: *"Here's my character (hero.png). Make her walk in 8 directions."* **To try it free, with no key**, ask Claude to *"try SpriteCast"*. An image model (OpenAI's, with your own key) does the drawing. The body, the motion, the angle and the shadow come from 3D - so every frame is the same person, and she actually walks. **Everything at one angle.** What makes an isometric game look AI-made is rarely one bad sprite - it is things seen from different cameras side by side: a character drawn from above, standing on a square tile laid flat, beside a front-on heart and potion from an icon pack. Draw everything at the same iso view and in the same light - the character, the trees and the ground, and also the heart and the potion she picks up, each from its own 3D model with its shadow - and the game stops looking pasted together. (What sits on the screen, like her hearts at the top, can stay front-on - drawn from the same 3D heart.) ![the same scene: on the left the game before - a square grass tile and a front-on heart and potion from an icon pack; on the right now - a 3D meadow, and the heart and potion made from 3D models at the game's angle, with their shadows](docs/one-angle.png) Free and MIT: you pay OpenAI and Tripo directly (1 Tripo credit = $0.01), nothing goes to the author, and every paid step shows its cost and waits for your OK. A walking character is about **$3** with its own 3D model - or about **$0.55** drawn on a mannequin, with no Tripo at all - a prop a few cents, a side-scroller's monster about **$0.18** - and the 3D guides, the finishing, the ground (a meadow, a path, puddles), the 3D shadows, see-through things, creatures' poses, the wind, the export to Phaser and Godot and the try cost nothing.
what each one costs | | you give | you get | about | |---|---|---|---| | **A walking character** | one illustration | a walk in 8 facings, standing views, a shadow per frame | **$2.9** (drawing $2.1 + Tripo $0.75) | | **A walking character on a mannequin** | a description and a picture from your game | a walk in 8 facings seen from above (or a side view), drawn on SpriteCast's own mannequin - no 3D model of it | **$0.54** ($0.06 the design + $0.06 a facing; as pixel art ~$1.2) | | **Another action** | a name (Tripo: quick), or a Mixamo FBX (more natural) | run, jump, slash, throw... in 8 facings | **$0.8-1.5** an action (drawing $0.7-1.4 + Tripo $0.10; an FBX: free) | | **Pixel art** | a character that walks | pixel sprites about 100 px tall | **$1.35** a walk in 8 facings ($0.075 a sheet) | | **An animal** | one illustration | a four-legged walk in 8 facings | **$2.8** (drawing $2.5 + Tripo $0.30) | | **A side-scroller's hero** | one illustration | a walk and standing seen from the side (one facing drawn, the other its mirror), her actions | **$1.1** (drawing $0.33 + Tripo $0.75), each action ~$0.3 | | **A side-scroller's monster or townsperson** | a description and a picture from your game | a design, a walk drawn on a mannequin's poses, a sheet of four moments (struck, falling apart) | **$0.18** ($0.06 a picture; no 3D model of it) | | **Sitting** | a character that walks | seated in 8 facings, placed on your props | **$0.22** (four facings: $0.11) | | **A prop, or a posed NPC** | a description | a sprite, its shadow, its anchor | **$0.08** (+ $0.09 a further facing) | | **A pixel-art prop** | a description | pixel sprites from every side, at the pixel character's scale | **$0.28** for one side (Tripo $0.20 + $0.08 a side) | These are the figures each script prints before it spends; the bills have come in a little under (a prop's drawing: $0.068).
**No API key? Draw in the ChatGPT app by hand.** `pixelart.py CHAR.json --manual` (or `SPRITECAST_DRAW=manual` for any step) calls no API and costs nothing: each sheet becomes a job on a local page (127.0.0.1:8790) that shows what to send. In a new ChatGPT chat (the free plan works, within its limits) you send two messages: first the reference pictures, which it only answers "ready" to, then the guide with the prompt. Save the answer, and it is taken from your Downloads folder by itself. Tried on Rain Girl's walk: with the guide alone, the same character in all 8 frames; with the references sent first (3 frames), the coat's buttons came out too. Still a little plainer than through the API, and a frame or two may need drawing again. ## What you can make ![a castle guard walking in 8 facings seen from above, each beside the plain mannequin whose walk he was drawn on](docs/mannequin-walk.gif)

No 3D model, no Tripo: a walk in 8 facings drawn on SpriteCast's own mannequin, from one design - about $0.55.

| | | |---|---| | ![walking in 8 facings](docs/character-walk.gif) | ![running, jumping and slashing with an umbrella](docs/actions.gif) | | **[A walk in 8 facings](docs/guide/characters.md#walking-characters)** from one illustration, a shadow per frame | **[Actions](docs/guide/characters.md#more-actions-run-jump-slash)**: run, jump, slash - or any Mixamo clip | | ![pixel-art sprites throwing snowballs five ways on an isometric floor](docs/pixel-throw.gif) | ![an orange tabby in a yellow raincoat walking in 8 facings](docs/animal-walk.gif) | | **[Pixel art](docs/guide/pixel-art.md)**, about 100 px tall, with things that are held and thrown | **[Four-legged animals](docs/guide/characters.md#four-legged-animals)**, with no bought rig | | ![the rain girl seated on ten different seats](docs/seats.png) | ![a ramen street cart as a 3D model from four sides, and the same four sides as pixel-art sprites](docs/pixel-props.png) | | **[Sitting](docs/guide/characters.md#sitting)** on your props, the armrest in front of her worked out in 3D | **[Pixel-art props](docs/guide/pixel-art.md#pixel-art-props-any-object-any-side)** from any side, at the character's scale | | ![a rattan peacock chair as pixel art under the sun, on a grey day, under a bare bulb, a lamp in front and behind it, and a big light above](docs/indoor-shadows.png) | ![a pixel-art tree from two sides swaying in the wind, clumps of leaves moving a pixel at a time](docs/sway.gif) | | **[Shadows baked from the 3D model](docs/guide/pixel-art.md#light-shadow-wind)**: the sun, a grey day, or a lamp you place | **[Wind in the leaves](docs/guide/pixel-art.md#light-shadow-wind)**, bough by bough, from the same model | | ![a side-scrolling game: the rain girl at the castle gate with a guard and a herbalist, a stone wolf on the wall-walk, a storm cloud over a wooden ledge](docs/side-game.png) | ![a stone wolf, a boar and a stag walking, each at its own step](docs/creature-walk.gif) | | **[A side-scrolling game](#a-side-scrolling-game-one-facing-and-monsters-drawn-in-2d)**: one facing drawn, the other its mirror | **[Monsters and people drawn in 2D](#a-side-scrolling-game-one-facing-and-monsters-drawn-in-2d)** on a mannequin's walk, no 3D model each | ## Things to ask for - *"Here's my character (hero.png). Make her walk in 8 directions."* - *"Add a run and a jump. And a throw - here's a Mixamo clip (Throw.fbx); put a snowball in her hand."* - *"Our game is pixel art. Make her walk and throw as pixel sprites, about 96 px tall."* - *"Make her sit, and put her on this armchair."* - *"Make a shopkeeper NPC, an old man in a brown cardigan, in four directions."* (a posed figure: a description is enough) - *"Make an isometric bookshelf, 1.8 m tall, full of books, in the cozy style."* - *"We're making a side-scroller. Make her walk and attack seen from the side."* - *"Make a wolf, a boar and a town guard for it - no 3D model for each."* ## Why it works An image model can't keep a body and a pose from one frame to the next. Asked for a walk in words, it gives eight nice drawings that don't walk: | GPT alone | SpriteCast | |---|---| | the same leg in front in all eight frames | the legs come from a 3D walk | | the arms twitch at random | the arms swing against the legs | | the camera at eye level | your game's camera (30° down by default) | | no shadow | the 3D body's own shadow, frame by frame | So SpriteCast never asks it to. **3D does the moving; the image model only redraws** each rendered frame in your illustration's look. Every drawing is fitted back onto its render and checked against it: a frame drawn in another pose is flagged and can be redrawn, never squeezed to fit. Props work the same way, with blocks at real size in place of the rig - so props made at different times line up on one floor, all lit by the same light. ## Made with it Two small games made as examples, each in about a day, with every picture from SpriteCast - to show what you can build with it. ### Rain Girl: isometric pixel art

▶ Play it in your browser  ·  the game's code
No install, no account. Post your score and you are on the board below.

Rain Girl, a small pixel action game: a girl in a yellow raincoat puts out fire monsters with her umbrella's water before the forest burns.

- **The girl.** One illustration; a Tripo model, rigged and rendered at the game's camera (2:1, 30° down): a walk with her umbrella, the swing and standing, in the four diagonal facin

repository.description: AI-native TypeScript game engine for AI agents, targeting all major platforms. WebGPU rendering, ECS, procedural assets, and a CLI-first development workflow.

details.readme:
**Language**: **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

ForgeAX Engine

AI-native TypeScript game engine — turn ideas into playable games.

AI agents are its primary users. Data, lifecycles, APIs, and tools serve one goal:
help AI understand the system, act precisely, inspect results, and repair failures.

Showcase · Features · Get started · AI efficiency · Architecture · Explore

> [!IMPORTANT] > **Efficiency is the goal; design is the method.** Complete more verified game-development work with less context, fewer failed attempts, and shorter feedback cycles. ## Made with ForgeAX Games built on the engine, authored through the `forgeax` CLI and an AI-first workflow.

Tiangong Warframe · Mecha action / 3D
My AI Companion Can't Be an Ancient Weapon Spirit! · ARPG / 3D

Pet Go-Karts · Racing / 3D
Rotten Farm

Browse the full showcase →

## Features - **Rendering** — Materials, lights, shadows, post-processing, GPU particles, trails, and beams on WebGPU - **Gameplay** — ECS world, 2D/3D physics (Rapier), animation, input, audio, and network sync - **Asset pipeline** — Import glTF / FBX / images, or generate assets in TypeScript with parameterized variants - **AI-first debugging** — Query live entities, record / replay render frames, and inspect draws down to pixels - **CLI workflow** — Create, run, inspect, and package games with `forgeax` commands - **Multi-platform** — Web, WeChat Mini Game, Steam, Steam Deck, Switch, and Kubee ## Get started With Node.js and pnpm available, install Engine from the development channel to create a project and open View. ```bash npm install -g @forgeax/engine@next forgeax project new my-game --template game-3d cd my-game forgeax dev start ``` To reproduce a specific setup, install the exact version from its release notes. See the [Engine package guide](packages/engine/README.md#create-a-project) for local package testing. `game-3d` is a third-person reference; `empty` is a minimal start. Read the generated README and skills, then see [Engine](packages/engine/README.md) and the [CLI guide](skills/forgeax-engine-cli/SKILL.md).
Run and verify ```bash pnpm exec forgeax help --tree --json pnpm exec forgeax project check pnpm exec forgeax dev status --json pnpm exec forgeax dev capture --json pnpm exec forgeax dev stop --json pnpm exec forgeax project test pnpm exec forgeax project package --format web-zip ``` Observations carry a `revision`; captures return PNG and report references. For entity lookup, camera control, and runtime identity constraints, see [persistent live control](packages/devkit/README.md#persistent-live-control).
Build from Engine source Toolchain versions are defined in [`.nvmrc`](.nvmrc), [`.pnpm-version`](.pnpm-version), and [`.bun-version`](.bun-version). ```bash pnpm install pnpm build:engine pnpm test ``` | Scenario | Entry | |:--|:--| | Public source checkout | Independent public source with `.forgeax-public-distribution` and prebuilt WASM; run the install / build commands above without private submodules | | Full contributor checkout | Clone with `--recurse-submodules` for authorized private asset access; run `pnpm build` for the complete application fleet | | Single demo iteration | `pnpm build:app hello/triangle`; broader acceptance follows the Smoke gate | `pnpm engine:pack --output ` builds the Engine npm archive under the 64 MB compressed size limit (64,000,000 bytes). The [authoring guide](skills/forgeax-engine-authoring/SKILL.md) covers game work. Both local and GitHub development releases publish this package under `next`. See the [release procedure](packages/engine/RELEASING.md).
## Prerequisites - **Node.js** ≥ 22.13.0 — [`.nvmrc`](.nvmrc) pins `22.22.3` - **pnpm** `12.10.1` via Corepack (`corepack enable`) - **Bun** ≥ 1.2.0 - A **WebGPU-capable browser** (latest Chrome / Edge) ## AI efficiency Efficiency means **verified useful work**, accounting for diagnosis and rework, context, and tool round trips. | Capability | How it improves AI efficiency | |:--|:--| | **Transparent rendering** | [RHI-debug](packages/rhi-debug/README.md) records and replays self-contained frames, exposing draw/dispatch work, bindings, resources, and pixels to locate incorrect inputs | | **Transparent runtime logic and data** | [ECS](packages/ecs/README.md) makes components, queries, and schedules explicit; [Remote](packages/remote/README.md) queries live instances to locate failures from actual state | | **Authorable, traceable assets** | [ScriptablePack / Pack](packages/pack/README.md) generate content in TypeScript or declare it in JSON; stable GUIDs connect sources and artifacts, with repair routed through the producer | | **Reversible plugin changes** | [Native Cordis](packages/plugin/README.md) unifies dependencies, activation, and cleanup; failed configuration updates can restore the last working Fiber | | **Measurable performance and results** | [Profiler](packages/profiler/README.md) provides bounded CPU captures and offline comparison; [Preview](packages/preview/README.md), browser captures, and project tests supply runtime evidence | | **CLI-first operation** | [DevKit](packages/devkit/README.md) unifies `forgeax` discovery, JSON input/output, and persistent instances for repeatable, composable operations | | **Context on demand** | [Skills](skills/), package contracts, and tool descriptions reveal only the knowledge needed for the task | | **Structured failure and recovery** | [`Result` and closed error unions](packages/types/README.md) provide codes, expectations, hints, and details; capabilities, execution tiers, and recovery state are explicit | > [!NOTE] > Screenshots, structural checks, and real GPU execution answer different questions. CPU captures cannot substitute for GPU performance measurements.
Design principles **Compression is intelligence: reduce the concepts needed to understand local behavior.** Avoid duplicate state, extra lifecycles, and implicit branches. | Design principle | How ForgeAX applies it | |:--|:--| | **AI is the primary user** | Prioritize discoverable, callable, verifiable machine contracts; AI usability takes precedence over human convention | | **One source of truth** | World owns game state, Renderer owns render projections, and source assets plus Meta own author facts; other layers consume or derive | | **Derive from declarations** | Material `paramSchema` derives layouts; RenderGraph derives dependencies and lifetimes from accesses; project declarations generate the Catalog | | **Compose within domain boundaries** | Physics, rendering, assets, and audio own their execution data; plugins assemble capabilities and ECS schedules frame work | | **Native lifecycle and unified cleanup** | Cordis `Context / Entry / Fiber` manage capability existence; `inject / provide / effect` express dependencies, services, and cleanup | | **Explicit states and failures** | Closed unions, structured errors, and reported capability absence and fallback reduce hidden branches | | **Prepare at build time, consume at runtime** | Import, WGSL composition and reflection, and VFX compilation produce published content for runtime loading | See the AI-first design axiom and module ownership map for the full constraints.
## Architecture **One authoritative World.** Runtime assembles services, Render maintains render projections, and build tools produce resources. ```mermaid flowchart TB PROJECT["Game project
forge.json · code · asset sources"] DEVKIT["DevKit / CLI
project operations · build · inspect"] COOK["Build-time production
import · cook · shader / VFX compilation"] ASSETS["AssetRegistry
GUID → published content"] APP["App + native Cordis
realm assembly · input · frame pacing · lifecycle"] WORLD["ECS World
state · time · Update / FixedUpdate"] DOMAINS["Domain systems
scene · animation · physics · audio intents · net"] RUNTIME["Runtime
select backends and services · assemble Renderer"] RENDER["Render
persistent projection · extract / prepare / record"] GRAPH["RenderGraph
resource accesses · pass dependencies · lifetimes"] RHI["RHI
opaque handles · capabilities"] GPU["rhi-webgpu / rhi-wgpu
browser WebGPU / wgpu WASM"] NULL["rhi-null
structural validation"] DEBUG["RHI-debug
capture · replay · inspect"] PROJECT --> DEVKIT DEVKIT --> COOK COOK --> ASSETS DEVKIT --> APP APP --> WORLD APP --> RUNTIME WORLD <--> DOMAINS RUNTIME --> RENDER WORLD -->|"Change evidence and scene data"| RENDER ASSETS --> RENDER RENDER --> GRAPH GRAPH --> RHI RHI --> GPU RHI --> NULL RHI -.->|"Optional recording"| DEBUG ```
Rendering and GPU | Subsystem | Key design and responsibility | Read more | |:--|:--|:--| | **Render / RenderGraph** | Persistent CPU projection and capability-gated GPU Scene; programmable pipelines and RenderFeatures; derived dependencies, usages, and lifetimes with raster / compute / copy passes executed in declaration order | [Render](packages/render/README.md) · [RenderGraph](packages/render-graph/README.md) | | **Shader / Material** | Schema-derived parameter and binding layouts; WGSL composition, Naga validation and reflection; runtime lookup of content-addressed compiled artifacts | [Shader](packages/shader/README.md) · [Compiler](packages/shader-co

repository.description: Open source previs software in the browser: block a scene, pose characters, author camera moves and cuts, then take the same shots to an AI video model.

details.readme:
English · 한국어 · 日本語 · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · Español · Français · Deutsch · Português (BR) · Русский

Make the scene first. Then make it a video.
Open source previs in a browser tab: block the set, move the cast, cut the camera, hand the shot to an AI video model.

Try it in the browser · Quick start · Guide for AI agents · Docs · Changelog · Discord

Top: the greybox blocked in CozyClay. Bottom: the AI video made from it. Same idea, a parkour jump: the blocking holds the timing and the camera.
## Why AI video costs money per take, and one miss means paying again. A text prompt cannot hold a whole scene: where everyone stands, how they move, where the camera is, when it cuts. CozyClay lets you make those decisions first, in 3D, where they are cheap to change. Then the video model gets the shot as a first frame, a greybox reference clip and a prompt that describes the real framing. It follows the blocking instead of guessing. ```mermaid flowchart LR S["Stage
set + cast"] --> M["Motion
written + built"] --> C["Camera
shots + cuts"] --> E["Export
frame · clip · prompt"] --> V["AI video model"] ``` ## Quick start ```bash npx cozyclay ``` That is the whole install. You need Node.js 22.19 or newer and a Chromium browser. You do not need a GPU, Python or a model download. The studio opens at `http://127.0.0.1:5180/app/`. **Updating.** - `npx cozyclay` fetches the newest release on every run. - After `npm install -g cozyclay`, the studio shows an **Update** chip in the top bar when a release is out. **Update now** installs it. **Restart now** starts the new version in the same terminal. - On Windows the chip shows the command to copy instead. One-click update stays off there by design. - `cclay update` does the same from the terminal. - Turn the check off for one launch with `--no-update-check` or `COZYCLAY_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`. Turn it off for good with `cclay update --off`, and back on with `cclay update --on`. > **Asking an AI agent to set it up?** Give it this repository link. Its instructions are in > [`INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md). ## What you can do | | | | --- | --- | | **Stage** | Build the set from primitives and place point, spot and directional lights. Add rig characters, drawn as cube figures, or capsule stand-ins when nobody needs to move a limb. Fly the view like a 3D editor. | | **Move** | Describe the action in the Agent panel. A second model, the motion writer, writes a motion spec, and a deterministic engine makes every frame and measures foot slide, contacts, balance and bodies inside props. The writer reads those numbers and contact sheets of the result before the take goes in. A motion can move props too. Runs and jumps follow captured human motion, sitting down, standing up and kneeling move the two legs apart, and a scene can hold a rope that is tied, draped, held and let go. It needs a model sign-in in the Agent panel. | | **Shoot** | Put shots on a timeline, draw dolly rails in the Top-View, look through the lens. Turn a rail camera by hand and pick who it follows. Each shot knows the limits of the video model you target. A shot camera can look straight down or straight up, and each camera key can choose how its move is eased. | | **Export** | Keyframe pack (first and last frame, greybox clip, camera, prompt), AI video reference zip (a mosaic-and-blur reference video and a prompt), mp4, depth and normal passes, contact sheet, OTIO cut list. | | **Look** | The toon look (flat two-tone shading with black lines) is on by default in the viewport and in every capture and export. Turn it off under **Show** in the viewport toolbar. | | **Undo anything** | Every edit, including each change the agent makes, is one undo step. | ## Direct it with AI The same scene can be driven from three places, live, while you watch the viewport. | Surface | Start | For | | --- | --- | --- | | **Agent panel** | `Cmd/Ctrl+B` in the studio | Chat in the studio. Sign in with ChatGPT or use your own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, MiniMax, OpenRouter, CLIProxyAPI). | | **MCP server** | `npx -y cozyclay mcp` | Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client. | | **Terminal** | `cclay live status --wait` | Coding agents that drive a running studio, JSON in and out. | ```json { "mcpServers": { "cozyclay": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "cozyclay", "mcp"] } } } ``` ## From source ```bash git clone https://github.com/HaD0Yun/CozyClay.git && cd CozyClay npm install npm run dev # http://127.0.0.1:5180/app/ npm test ``` Contribution rules are in [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). Open pull requests against `main`. ## Docs | Read | For | | --- | --- | | [`INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md) | Install, run and connect, written for AI agents | | [`docs/motion3-agent-guide.md`](docs/motion3-agent-guide.md) | The old motion engine (MCP, `cclay live`, `COZYCLAY_MOTION_ENGINE=old`): motion specs, compile and QA | | [`docs/agent-cli.md`](docs/agent-cli.md) | `cclay live`, model providers, sessions | | [`mcp/README.md`](mcp/README.md) | MCP tools and the live protocol | | [`docs/studio-ui-ia.md`](docs/studio-ui-ia.md) | Every control and where it lives | | [`docs/privacy.md`](docs/privacy.md) | Anonymous telemetry and how to turn it off (`cclay telemetry off`) | | [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) | Contribution rules | ## Guides | Read | For | | --- | --- | | [Greybox to AI video](https://cozyclay.org/greybox-to-video/) | Why a grey blockout is the most reliable input for a video model, and the block-then-generate loop | | [Previs software compared](https://cozyclay.org/previs-software/) | Free, open source and browser-based previs tools side by side | | [Seedance 2.5 camera control](https://cozyclay.org/seedance-camera-control/) | Getting the same camera on every take with a reference clip | | [Camera control for AI video](https://cozyclay.org/ai-camera-control/) | Why camera prompts drift and what the models actually accept | Found a bug or want a feature? [Open an issue](https://github.com/HaD0Yun/CozyClay/issues). ## License AGPL-3.0-or-later. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE), [`LICENSING.md`](LICENSING.md) and [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Made by [Doyun](https://github.com/HaD0Yun) at [NomaDamas](https://github.com/NomaDamas).

details.readme:
# Castwright

![Castwright — any book, performed by a full cast, kept true, kept yours, book after book](public/og.png)

> _Any book, performed by a full cast — kept true, kept yours, book after book._

**▶ Hear a 90-second sample** — the same passage as one narrator, then the full cast: **[castwright.ai/#demo](https://www.castwright.ai/#demo)**.

Turn a manuscript into a finished, **full-cast** audiobook on your own machine —
every character in their own voice, consistent across a whole series. Castwright
runs locally end-to-end; with no cloud analyzer key set, nothing leaves your
computer.

Upload `.md` / `.txt` / `.epub` / `.pdf` / `.mobi` / `.azw3` → an analyzer
extracts characters, chapters, and per-sentence speaker tags → assign a voice to
each character → generate per-chapter audio → listen, revise, and export to M4B
or MP3.

## What you get

- **Full-cast performance** — every character speaks in their own voice; one
  narrator can't be everyone.
- **Series memory** — a character keeps the same voice across every book in a
  series, even when an author renames someone mid-series. *(No other tool does
  this for readers.)*
- **Designed voices** — every character gets a unique voice designed from its persona (Qwen3-TTS), kept consistent across the series; Kokoro ships a ready-made catalogue alongside it. (Cloning a voice from your own sample is the next major release.)
- **Seven languages** — performs English, Russian, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, and Japanese end-to-end, with the manuscript's language detected on import. A cast never crosses languages within a book. (CJK attribution leans on the analyzer model — a local Qwen analyzer is recommended for Chinese and Japanese.)
- **Quality-checked automatically** — every chapter is gated before it's assembled: acoustic checks (dead air, over-long lines, timing drift), optional word-for-word ASR transcript verification, and an opt-in speaker-fingerprint check that catches a voice drifting out of character even when the words are right. Flagged takes are surfaced on the waveform and re-recorded automatically.
- **On-device by default** — speech is always local. The analyzer is local too;
  add a cloud key and it falls back to the cloud automatically unless you switch
  that off.
- **Listen on your phone or tablet** — an Android companion app plays from your library over your home network, opening into a two-pane layout on tablets and foldables. Chapters you haven't downloaded play instantly on-network, with no OS certificate install.
- **You own the files** — export standard M4B (cover and chapter markers), MP3, AAC/M4A or Opus, a native **Audiobookshelf** export (series metadata, `metadata.json`, and a folder cover), and SRT/VTT captions (per sentence or per line, whole-book or per-chapter). EBU R128 loudness normalisation is on by default. No lock-in.

## Documentation

The full user guide — installing, uploading a book, casting, generating
audio, listening, exporting, and every feature area — lives on the
[wiki](https://github.com/dudarenok-maker/Castwright/wiki), illustrated
with real screenshots.
